System / Application: BYOA Agent Platform (/opt/v6) on host gx10-040e: the signing check shared by 7 agents (fx, summarize, match, offensive-text, rag-retrieve, webcrawl, websearch)
Technology / Component: byoa_adk: the shared toolkit that checks each request's digital signature (file byoa_adk/security.py)
Advisory / Vulnerability ID: None. This is a design weakness we found ourselves, so it has no CVE number.
Description / Evidence: Every request to an agent carries a digital signature, like a wax seal on a letter, to prove it came from the platform. The problem: the seal covers only the task ID, goal ID, capability name and time, and NOT the actual data being sent (the 'inputs'). So someone could open the letter, change the data, and the seal still looks valid. Also, a valid request can be sent again and again for 5 minutes, because nothing marks a request as 'already used'. We tested this on the real code: (1) a request with a valid signature but changed data was accepted (HTTP 200) and the changed data was processed; (2) the same signed request was accepted a second time.
Internet-Facing? (Yes/No/Unknown): Unknown. The agents listen on all network addresses, but we could not confirm they are reachable from the internet.
Exposure / Exploitability: An attacker would first need to see or intercept a real signed request (for example by sniffing unencrypted traffic or from a log), then change the data or resend it within 5 minutes. They cannot run code on the agent or forge a brand-new request from nothing.
Business Impact: Someone who gets hold of a real request could change what an agent works on (for example, the text to summarize or the figures to match) or make the agent repeat a task. That could lead to wrong results in finance or AP workflows, with nobody noticing.
Current Controls: The signature itself is strong (HMAC-SHA256). Requests older than 5 minutes are rejected. Each agent only accepts the capabilities it declares. Inputs are checked against a schema. Rejected requests are written to an audit log.
Remediation / Mitigation Action: 1) Make the signature also cover the request data, by including a fingerprint (SHA-256 hash) of the inputs. 2) Give every request a one-time ID and remember used IDs for a few minutes, so a replay is refused. 3) Shorten the 5-minute window. 4) Update the platform controller (which creates the signatures) and all agents together, since old and new signing will not match. Bump the ADK version.
Verification Evidence / Link: Test script in the scratchpad: adktest/r.py. Before the fix it prints 'orig 200', then the changed data accepted, then 'replay again 200'. After the fix, both the changed-data and the replayed request must be refused with 401.
Notes: Found by reading the code, then confirmed with a test. Escalate because the fix changes how every agent and the controller talk to each other, so it must be rolled out together. We have not checked whether traffic between the controller and agents is encrypted (TLS); if it is not, the risk is higher.
